title: Lattice basket (Gitterwerk)
lede: Josef Hoffmann’s basket for the Wiener Werkstätte is cut from plated sheet metal perforated with a grid of squares, so the grid is the whole structure and the only ornament.
summary: Nickel-plated metal pierced with a square grid, with a stepped handle. Josef Hoffmann for the Wiener Werkstätte, c. 1905–1910.

evidence.note: Downloaded the Minneapolis Institute of Art photograph of object 98.276.65 (800 × 598 px) to a scratch folder and inspected it. It is not stored. Other museums hold silver and painted versions of Hoffmann’s lattice baskets that differ in shape, for example the [Chazen Museum of Art, 2012.32.3.2a-b](https://chazen.wisc.edu/collection/24790/gitterwerk-basket/), which I did not inspect.

styles.note: A clear example of Hoffmann’s square lattice (Gitterwerk), the object type behind his nickname “Quadratl-Hoffmann”.

context: Mia records the basket as designed by Josef Hoffmann and made by the Wiener Werkstätte, c. 1905–10, in nickel-plated brass, 15.24 × 26.04 × 13.97 cm to the handles, marked “Wiener Werkstätte / JH”. [Mia 98.276.65](https://collections.artsmia.org/art/7097/basket-josef-hoffmann).

Mia’s label: Hoffmann designed various household objects in gitterwerk, or gridwork; the gridded sheets of base metal were the structure of the objects as well as their decoration, and they were made affordably and often nickel- or silver-plated. [Mia 98.276.65](https://collections.artsmia.org/art/7097/basket-josef-hoffmann).
Koloman Moser designed objects in the same technique; see [Moser’s lattice bud vase](ref:moser-gitterwerk-bud-vase).
observed: The basket is a low vessel of bright plated metal pierced with a regular grid of square holes.
In plan the wall steps in and out in shallow curves and corners, so the grid bends around a scalloped outline.
A flat lattice handle rises in straight segments and steps down at each side, like a stepped arch.
The top edge and the base are plain metal strips; every other surface is grid.
interpretation: The grid is used as a material, like a fabric, and the shape comes from folding it. This is the plainest statement of the square as the module of the style.
The shine of the plating is the one luxury. In a flat design the same effect can come from a gold or silver line.
borrow: Use a square-hole grid as a full panel texture with a plain border strip at the top and bottom.
Step a frame line in right-angled segments instead of curving it.

rights.statement: No image is stored. Mia gives the rights status as Unknown. Josef Hoffmann died in 1956, so his designs are protected in Austria until the end of 2026.
